Job Opening: Draftsman/Work Planner 
SRBA Interior is looking for an enthusiastic and experienced Draftsman/Work Planner . 
About SRBA Interior 
SRBA Interior, a division of the SRBA Group, creates large-scale custom interiors for hotels, healthcare facilities, retail environments, and educational institutions, among others. With a strong combination of traditional craftsmanship and efficient production capacity, we have the flexibility to carry out both large-scale projects and unique, specialized custom solutions. From concept to completion, we work closely with clients, architects, and developers. 
Job Description 
At SRBA Interior, you'll work as a Production Planner/Drafter on challenging and prestigious interior design projects, such as those for The Sting, Costes, and the Cotton Club. You'll be responsible for preparing, developing, and creating technical drawings for custom interiors and furniture. 
With an eye for detail, you'll ensure that designs are translated into clear production drawings and practical solutions for the workshop and installation teams. You'll work closely with clients, architects, the workshop, and the installation department to ensure projects run smoothly. 
You'll be part of a close-knit and professional team where quality, precision, and collaboration are key. You'll ensure that every project is well-prepared and successfully brought from concept to finished product. 
We ask: - You are a skilled draftsman/work planner - You have an eye for quality and take pride in delivering high-quality, professional work - You have experience with technical drawing and/or work planning - You have experience with drafting software such as AutoCAD and Palette CAD - You have technical knowledge of materials, structures, and manufacturing processes - You are detail-oriented, solution-oriented, and skilled at planning and collaborating - You are fluent in English

 Introduction 
The Scholar Meeting of International Tax Researchers (ScholarMIT) is an annual gathering in our Amsterdam Headquarters where early-career tax scholars can discuss their ongoing projects amongst contemporaries in the field. 
 Description 
The Scholar Meeting of International Tax Researchers (ScholarMIT) is designed for early-career tax scholars who have obtained their PhD and are under the age of 50. 
This event, held at the IBFD Head Office in Amsterdam on 1-2 February 2027, provides a dynamic platform for researchers to discuss their ongoing projects, receive expert coaching, and exchange innovative ideas with colleagues from around the world. What is the eligibility criteria? 
A maximum of 12 researchers will be admitted, selected based on the quality and originality of their research. We are looking for applicants who: 
• Applicants must spend at least 30% of their work time on research-related activities. 
• Be developing an innovative research project on international, European, or comparative taxation. 
• University professors and lecturers are particularly encouraged to apply. How do you apply? 
Upload a short CV, a synopsis of your research ( use this template ), and your PhD certificate at this link by 1 September 2026. 
• Selected participants will be announced by 15 September 2026. 
• Final materials are due by 1 December 2026. Venue 
IBFD office, Amsterdam

Looking for a stable production job with good pay where you work with your hands? We are hiring Production Workers for the Core Making department at MGG in Tegelen. In this department, you produce sand cores that are used to make high-quality aluminum castings for industries like automotive, energy, and medical equipment. This is a hands-on job in a 3-shift system, including night shifts. This job is a good fit if you: Live near Tegelen and have your own accommodation and transport Have experience working in a 3-shift system (or at least night shifts) Speak English, German, or Dutch Experience as a Production Worker or Operator is a plus, but motivation and reliability are more important.
